steps.content: The Dark Side of DisCity: Rule of Shadow [Revised Edition] [Unpublished]

<size=40>Historical analysis indicates the corruption of the Independence Army was a multifactorial process.

Economically, both the demands of warfare against the metropole coalition and the subsequent need to rebuild the city-state under trade blockades required immense capital and resources.

<size=40>Following key military successes, the Independence Army's influence expanded, drawing corporations and wealthy industrialists into its orbit. These alliances provided necessary financial support for the war and initial reconstruction.

Through their involvement in rebuilding, these allied groups steadily consolidated control over the city-state's critical economic infrastructure.
Contemporary records suggest neither Dravyn nor the Army's command possessed the administrative experience to perceive the systemic risk.

<size=40>This, truly, was the origin and root of everything.
Yet, compared to the dramatic political shifts, personal betrayals, and fallen heroes that followed, these mundane economic origins were largely obscured in the historical narrative.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If DisCity's blade ever starts to break—if you ever verge on rampage—I will find you. I will stop you. I'll do whatever it takes to make you stand down... even if it means following the path you took when you killed Dravyn with your own hands.
...Haunted by that person's strange words, Augustus returns home. She seeks solace in the pages of a book, but as she reads, the lines begin to blur, lulling her into a peculiar dream.

?? ??, N.F. 103
Cryogenic Chamber, ???? Laboratory
...It hurts...
Where am I...? EDGE?
Her body was a foreign, leaden weight, and it took a monumental strain of will just to try sitting up.
Ugh, these side effects are bad... That baldy's cryogenic tech is complete garbage... He'd better hope his tech didn't fry a single nerve...
Finally, she managed it.
Outside the cryogenic chamber, there were no researchers or military officers waiting.
Instead, she was met with a sea of blood.
...Did they forcibly awaken me...? What happened?
Is this a battlefield? Where is the enemy? When did the war begin?
Who are you?!

steps.speaker: Iron Mask
steps.content: I'm the new Rancor wielder.
<color=#7683a2><i>...Another replacement?
<color=#7683a2><i>But... he explicitly promised he wouldn't use those again...
<color=#7683a2><i>Did Dravyn send you?

steps.speaker: Iron Mask
steps.content: The Marshal is in a dire situation. He awakened you in hopes you might be of use.

steps.speaker: Iron Mask
steps.content: This is his order to you.
A top-secret directive awaited the awakened one, its encryption a cypher unused since the fires of the Independence War had cooled.

<size=40>[Excerpt 2]
From a contemporary historical viewpoint, Dravyn's political era effectively concluded with the Eclipse Operation in N.F. 103.

The operation was a catastrophic and strategically meaningless defeat, resulting in significant FAC casualties in the DisSea. The public outcry prompted an official investigation by EDGE.
Though it was largely overlooked at the time, the majority of the lost personnel were remnants of the former DisCorps. While Dravyn had previously survived numerous political challenges, the circumstances of this event created an inescapable predicament.

<size=40>Dravyn Steel, then FAC Commander-in-Chief, was politically isolated and subsequently died. The official cause of death was listed as complications from long-term depression. Contemporary accounts speculated it was a suicide driven by despair and the prospect of prosecution. More conspiratorial narratives alleged an assassination framed as a form of retribution.
The consensus among analysts is that for an authoritarian leader of his stature, only death would have compelled him to cede power.

<size=40>However, all these theories are difficult to reconcile with his documented, resolute character. The evidence suggests he was too formidably entrenched to be easily eliminated by external forces.

<size=40><color=#fb9259><i>
The Rancors are yours now. Wage war as you see fit.

<size=50>I only demand victory.
</color></size>
...What kind of order is this supposed to be?
Where is Dravyn?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Where is he?!

<size=40>[Excerpt 3]
The Marshal's career reveals a consistent pattern of tactical pragmatism.

Willing to sacrifice conscience and moral boundaries, he pursued victory at all costs, using success to justify every means. This approach characterized the campaign to counter nuclear assault, the suppression of dissenting city-states, and the neutralization of internal opposition.

<size=40>Confronted with an untenable situation, his response was operationally consistent. He authorized proscribed protocols, demonstrating a systematic disregard for collateral damage.
This calculus was applied universally, to adversaries and his own forces alike.
[Enter Flashback]

steps.speaker: Parma
steps.content: What's past is past, Marshal. What you need now... is help. Power.

steps.speaker: Parma
steps.content: So take it. Summon it again. The Sage's power is already in your hands. It chose you once. It won't let you die. Wield it. Defend your throne like you defended your city.

steps.speaker: Parma
steps.content: Where is that conviction now? Weren't you the one who said all power is justified if it serves your cause? Look at yourself, trapped, desperate... Isn't this your only option?

steps.speaker: Parma
steps.content: ...You said you refused to surrender, didn't you? So then... why hesitate? Heh heh... heh...
[Exit Flashback]

<size=40>[Excerpt 4]
Did no one try to stop him? The historical record suggests otherwise.
One does not achieve such stature by acting entirely alone against all counsel. A hero forged in the fires of the Independence War could never have been a mere isolated fanatic.

<size=40>And indeed, he was not alone. There were many who stood with him.
Shared ideals brought them together; a common enemy united them; collective suffering forged their bond.

But then victory arrived. The hardships ended, the enemy scattered, and the founding ideals were, on the surface, achieved. And with that, everything changed.

<size=40>We see the first fractures: internal division and collusion with the old power structures. The parasites of the former regime taught these new heroes how to feast, subtly pulling them into the same corrupt currents.
Those who refused to partake were methodically removed.

Victor was the first to fall, a man of political genius but no military skill, cleverly reassigned to the front lines where he "perished in combat."
The opposition chose their target well; without his unifying influence, the military's integrity began to crumble.
The steadfast Adrian held his principles to the end, but what was the purpose? A loyal advisor, once stripped of trust, is rendered useless.

<size=40>As for his family...

All eyes inevitably turned to the Steel family. Each member represented a potential vulnerability, a point of pressure. They shared Dravyn's blood, but few, it seems, could share his formidable vision or his resolve.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Greetings, General Augustus. Your vitals indicate severe stress from the forced awakening. For your physiological stability, I must insist you return to the cryogenic chamber.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Please rest assured. The city-state's security architecture remains optimal. Our military assets have been successfully realigned toward catastrophe prevention, and lingering societal instabilities are being systematically resolved. Progress is incremental, but with a more powerful EDGE, we will guide it to the correct path.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: It was you... you used him. You repurposed the entire DisCorps under the guise of catastrophe prevention, consolidating your control... The FAC program was just another one of your schemes...

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: You set him up as a figurehead, stripped him of any real power, and then spent nineteen years backing him into a corner!

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Violence and power are a mechanism, not an objective. All actions have been calculated for the preservation of the collective. The DisCorps restructuring was a necessary measure. I regret that more optimal solutions were not computationally viable. But regarding Marshal Dravyn...

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: He was provided with multiple viable paths. The one he selected led to his own termination.
Magnetic force erupted with her fury, pinning Schorl. The black triangle jerked and spasmed against her unyielding grip.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Stop hiding behind this cold, logical garbage! Show yourself and face me! COME OUT!!

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Logically—bzzt—this interface is no different—however, if a familiar form facilitates your compliance—
Despite its reluctance, EDGE complied with her demand, projecting the face of someone familiar before her eyes.

steps.speaker: EDGE-01
steps.content: Hello, General Augustus. It's been thirty-one years since we last met.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: What happened after I went under? In N.F. 84... No, even before that... what happened between you? How did it all come to this?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Were all the oaths we swore back then just... a pile of bullshit?!
His smile was a cold, detached thing, utterly foreign to the one she knew.

steps.speaker: EDGE-01
steps.content: I posed that same question to him once. I no longer trouble myself with such concerns.

steps.speaker: EDGE-01
steps.content: I recommend you also de-prioritize these concerns. Technical and logistical support remain available to you, should you require it.

steps.speaker: EDGE-01
steps.content: Or... would you prefer if I called you little Catherine again? Would that help soothe your emotions?
A blue light flashed, and in its wake, both his projection and the black triangle unraveled, vanishing without a trace.
[Scene Change: FAC Interior]

<size=40>[Excerpt 5]
Dravyn was not personally motivated by material gain. However, years of suppression by the metropoles fostered a deeply ingrained DisCity-centrism, a strategic vulnerability that proved highly exploitable.
The interests standing behind him, seeking to wield his authority for resource acquisition, consistently provided him with rationalized justifications for their campaigns.

<size=40>
In the era before the DisSea Explosion, the cause was the liberation of metropole colonies; this was used to legitimize the suppression of city-states that resisted DisCity's hegemony.
Following the explosion, the threat of Mania became the new justification, with the argument being that since DisCity had borne the primary impact, all of humanity was obligated to support its lead in combating the catastrophe.

<size=40>Consequently, with the commander's own focus shifted, the institution that revered and followed him was inevitably corrupted in turn.
It must be remembered that the former DisCorps was a highly systematic and methodical apparatus—a perfect machine for the dissemination and amplification of its leader's ideology.

<size=40>
The sword that a power forges for external dominance will, in time, be turned inward.

steps.speaker: Lieutenant
steps.content: General Augustus... Do you remember me?

steps.speaker: Lieutenant
steps.content: I see... Not as Lieutenant... but by my real name. I... I'm honored, General. And ashamed.

steps.speaker: Lieutenant
steps.content: This is the sword you entrusted to the Major. Now, it should return to your hands. The Eighth Division... I'm the only one left. Returning this to you is the only purpose my survival has left.

steps.speaker: Lieutenant
steps.content: What is our next objective, General? A civil war? Just as Marshal Dravyn said? Or are we to bleed another city dry, all to fund his political purges? How many more must we kill?

steps.speaker: Lieutenant
steps.content: ...I apologize, General. That was insubordinate. Seeing you again... it brought everything back.

steps.speaker: Lieutenant
steps.content: It makes no difference... Civil war or campaign, just give the order. Tell me who to kill. I can no longer hold a gun with pride anymore, but fighting for you... that I can still do.

steps.speaker: Lieutenant
steps.content: Seeing the fire still in your eyes, General... It's a relief.
[Scene Change: Cabinet Meeting Room 2]

<size=40>[Excerpt 6]
Is history unjust? One cannot help but wonder, watching the endless repetition of malevolence.

<size=40>
And yet, history possesses a certain grim fairness. Those who dare to abandon Justice... often find themselves collectively condemned, cast into the abyss.

<size=40>
But who, in the end, is fit to deliver the final verdict?

The young general finally reached the old commander's throne. The audience hall stood vast and empty, a void of such scale it bordered on absurdity. The round council table of her memories, with the many chairs that had once surrounded it, was gone. Only the solitary seat of authority remained.

The old man upon it was as motionless as stone. It was only the sound of her footsteps that made him stir, his body trembling slightly as he turned toward the young figure before him, awakening from his long trance.

He was awake now, but his face was so aged she barely recognized him. In the years unknown to her, Dravyn seemed to have borne the weight of mountains. The man who was once iron-hard and formidable now sat with a broken spine beneath his burdens.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: ...You're late... I didn't teach you to keep a battlefield waiting...

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: ...How did you get so old?

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: Me? Heh... I don't even remember what I looked like before old age claimed me.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: You, on the other hand, look exactly as I remember.

His clouded eyes, sunk deep in wrinkled furrows, trembled unsteadily before they slowly, painstakingly found their focus on the young general. He studied her in silence for a long moment before he finally spoke in a hushed voice.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: Has it really been that long...

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Why did you wake me?

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: I woke you...? Ah, yes... because we agreed to...

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: When the shadow of war returned... you would be the blade to meet it. To bring us victory.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: That time is now, Augustus... War is at our doorstep again. Defeat the enemies. Bring back victory, for me. Only you can do it.
Augustus remained silent for a moment before speaking deliberately.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: What war? DisCity is thriving. Its satellite town network is a deterrent. No foreign power would be so foolish.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Dravyn... what war are you talking about?

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: It's here. In this very city... The battlefield is everywhere...

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Then point me at your enemy. Where are they?

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: Where aren't they...? Beyond this room... everyone. Everyone is the enemy. Can't you see?
His eyes widened slightly, staring into some unseen distance. His hunched frame leaned forward slowly, as if his very soul were being drawn out, and his gaze filled with a bitter, consuming hatred.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: The enemies I thought I'd defeated... they just changed their faces after the war. Those I believed were my allies... once they left the battlefield, they put on new masks.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: They smile to my face, and the moment my back is turned, they plot. All of them. Just waiting for a crack in the armor, a sign of weakness. They don't want to serve this city; they want my chair.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: And the people... short-sighted, foolish, greedy, selfish! So easily led to break what they should be protecting... And assassins?? The Eclipse Operation's failure is my fault? We built this city from ash and sacrifice. And this... this is their gratitude?!

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: Is this my judgment? Or this city's? After all I've sacrificed to hold it together... what is the purpose of this... this Mania?

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: Oh yes, of course, I've known all along. That too is part of the enemy's conspiracy...
The old man continued to mumble incoherently under his breath.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: The Underground Mania, the shackles, the Shepherd... All lies. Waving a flag for "humanity" while they send my last loyal soldiers to die... burn my bridges...

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: EDGE has fallen... into their hands, corrupted by those depraved hounds. Even... even he has turned...

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: Or... was it always <color=#fb9259>his</color> plan...?

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: It was him all along... All that talk of fighting catastrophes, building the FAC together... Hah. Noble words. A disguise. It was just a slow, deliberate transfer of power. A trap to erode my authority!

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: He called himself a scientist. Said he understood my vision!

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: We had an agreement. To correct our errors. He said there was still time. For <color=#dg1f1f>nineteen years</color> I compromised. I trusted him. And this is when he moves against me?! <color=#dg1f1f><size=44><i>Then he will regret it!!</color></size><i>

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: This is MY DisCity. I took over the command, and I'm not giving it up. The victory I want will come, one way or another!

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: Augustus, I am the one who woke you! So take up your blade and cut down every last one of my enemies! Go! Forge more glory!

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: Only the shock of victory can crush these scheming vermin. Only undeniable strength forces obedience. Seize that victory; it is your purpose!

The aged marshal grew more fervent with each word, his voice swelling as if chasing the ghost of his former glory. He leaned forward, eagerly extending a hand toward Augustus, his sole audience member in the empty hall.
But he was met with utter silence.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: ...But this is not a war.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: What you're asking me to do is just clear the path, for you and you alone.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: You only want my blade to guard your throne.
Her answer was swallowed by a wave of unhinged laughter.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: HAHAHAHA! Since when did an Andohar preach to me about justice? Do you think I don't know who you really are?

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: You were born in a metropole. Your house built its fortune on war. Your loyalty was never to a flag; it was to war itself. So why not fight for me? I am giving you a battlefield of your own. Isn't that what you've always wanted? That has never changed!

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: ...You're right. No one has my loyalty. And I don't fight for banners...

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: But did you give that same order... to my soldiers?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: When you asked them to trust you, ordered them to die for you, did they know what they were really dying for?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: If Victor were here... what would he say?
He fell silent. Did that name still hold meaning for him? Did he still remember the comrades who had once pulled him back from the abyss?

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: Victor was murdered... I am avenging him.

steps.speaker: Thank you, I'm feeling fine... May I ask where Miss Stewart is?
steps.content: And Adrian? You stripped his rank yourself. You cast him out.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: Was he ever loyal? He always challenged my authority. Stood against me like a stone wall when I needed him most. That man... that bastard... he became an enemy long ago.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Who told you that? Your inner circle? Lapdogs who only know how to pledge loyalty? Or just a bunch of... bootlicking sycophants?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Do you really believe their loyalty? Or just the lies that comfort you?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Where are all those eager voices now?

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: The ones I could trust are all dead!!

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: You've never held command. You've never sat in this chair. You've never seen a real battlefield! Those enemies are undying ghosts... they can't be routed, can't be purged, more persistent than war itself...

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: This war permits no innocence, but they refused to see it! Adrian, Victor... neither of them could understand!

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: For this city—for all we've sacrificed—if I fail now, all those people's deaths will mean nothing! This is necessary! Can't you see that?!

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: ...I don't see it. And I don't want to. Haven't you already left behind what was truly necessary?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Those who give their lives for DisCity must not be betrayed by it. Those who fight for you must not be abandoned by their commander.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Brock entrusted you with the Independence Army. He told you to remember. But look around now, Dravyn...

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Who's still standing by your side?
A long silence settled between them. Augustus held the old marshal's gaze, watching as the final embers of passion guttered and died within his eyes.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: ...I see. So you, too, will stand against me...

The old man turned away and shuffled back toward the hall's only remaining chair. This was the commander who had once been the very embodiment of invincibility in her eyes. How could he have been reduced to this? How could a figure of such power become so diminished?

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: It seems... even you believe I've already lost...
Dravyn seemed to have aged years in moments, again, left with nothing but two things to which he desperately clung:
The dilapidated chair that only resembled a throne, and the Mania Rancor in his hand that was never a true blade to wield.
He clutched them as if they could anchor him, but time surged anyway, a torrent rushing through the spaces between his fingers.
[Flashback 1]

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Take care of my troops. They're my pride.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: You have my word.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: It doesn't matter. At least you still understand me... For victory, I would pay any price. Bear any burden.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: I will not yield... I will not allow DisCity to fall to <color=#fb9259>them</color>... This blight upon the city, this rot threatening my command... I... will not... abandon this post... I will not retreat...

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: Even if I must stand alone...
[Flashback 2]

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Well then, goodbye. I'll be waiting for the day I wake up.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: I'll be waiting for that day too.
Mania spilled from his gun barrel, unfurling like crimson petals and injecting his withered frame with a deceptive, frenzied vitality.

With this, Dravyn Steel descended into madness, fully merging with the Rancor. He was the second commander of the Independence Army, Eastside's first democratically elected Speaker, and the founder and first Commander-in-Chief of the FAC. He was the sole hero who had led DisCity from nuclear devastation, and in Andohar's eyes, its most tenacious and obsessive warrior. Now, he was none of these things, and he was mad.

In his final moment of lucidity, his gaze drifted down from his perch, and he recognized the figure before him one last time—just as he had futilely tried to distinguish friend from foe for the past thirty years.
<i>Ah... it's that brat. She's back... Well then... he should at least force a smile.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: ...I should have woken you sooner... but back then...

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: I believed I could give you a better world...

Dravyn stood upon his throne as he always wished, transformed into a weapon, and left before him the sharpest general of the Independence Army—the one he had personally summoned back from the past—now slowly raising her sword against him.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: ...Then why don't you just come back... you old jerk...
It was not a difficult battle.
It did not take long to kill a hero in his twilight years.
Augustus walked out of the hall alone. The sun had just dipped below the horizon, its final afterglow staining the distant sky.
Yet she could no longer tell what time of day it was, or even what year.
[Scene Change: Street]
Walking through the streets, she saw the same crowds who had once lined the roads celebrating victory and praising heroic soldiers now angrily demanded peace and justice, calling for a reckoning.

steps.speaker: Civilian
steps.content: My grandfather was just an innocent Outlander, and you killed him! You ****ing murdered him!! Don't you dare hide behind your DisCorps uniform and call yourselves heroes! We know what you did! You're not soldiers; you're butchers! Go to hell!!

steps.speaker: Civilian
steps.content: All this time... we lived beside them. We broke bread with them. To think such monsters were walking among us... I can't... I can't bear it. How do you live next to a demon?!

steps.speaker: Terrified Civilian
steps.content: Stay back! Get away from me! Please... don't kill me!
[Scene Change: Banquet/Hall]

Walking through the grand halls, she recognized the same parasites who were supposed to have been expelled by the Independence Army. They had merely changed their skins, and there they were, still clinging to the top. These were the ones who, after seizing a precious blade, had instigated wars for profit and slipped away unscathed. And now, they raised their glasses in celebration of a new era.

steps.speaker: Upper-Class Guest
steps.content: A toast! To the final exorcism of the old era's demons, and to the unequivocal correction of past errors! With the city-state firmly back on its proper course, we can finally usher in a future of stability and progress. An era of peace, led by our own steady hand!

steps.speaker: Fraser Caravan
steps.content: Of course! A new dawn has arrived. Let peace line our pockets, and prosperity build our legacy! To wealth, and to a future where business can truly flourish!
[Scene Change: Base]
Back on the battlefield, the soldiers she had once taken pride in were still there, waiting for her.

steps.speaker: Despairing Soldier
steps.content: General... is it really you? All these years... What happened to us? Tell me I wasn't wrong. We had to fight. DisCity... it would have fallen without us, wouldn't it?

steps.speaker: Despairing Soldier
steps.content: They told us... the enemy was at the gates! That the whole world wanted the Hypercubes we had. We were just securing resources... pre-empting the threat. People die in war; it's a cost we've accepted! I did it for our home... for our city-state! What was I supposed to do?!

steps.speaker: Despairing Soldier
steps.content: So then... was it wrong? Was I wrong? When did it... change? Or... was it always like this? Have I just been... a murderer all along?

steps.speaker: Despairing Soldier
steps.content: Then why did they pin medals on my chest?! Why did they call me a hero?! You were the ones who told us! That to fight for DisCity was the highest honor! That to kill for its future was glorious! I didn't—! I never wanted this! Not like this!!

steps.speaker: Despairing Soldier
steps.content: General... I only ever wanted to serve my city-state. Now... after all of it... is there really nothing waiting for me but hell?

Their glory was erased, their faces awash with confusion, helplessness, fear, and shame. The once-sharpest blades had proven the most brittle; those who had burned their lives for their beliefs now watched as those convictions shattered at reality's slightest touch, crumbling to dust.

So easily broken, so thoroughly abandoned, they were left to rust on meaningless battlefields. They were swallowed by the very war they served, living a fate worse than death, rejected even by hell itself.
What are you fighting for?

steps.speaker: Scarface
steps.content: It wasn't like that, Lily... Your brother's no murderer. I'm a soldier. A hero... It was the only way to keep you safe... Everything... it was all to keep you safe...

steps.speaker: Scarface
steps.content: GYAHAHAHAH!! Yes!! A hero!! Anyone who lays a finger on you deserves death! Every last one of those bloodstained hounds will die!! Those rabid dogs will never get near you!! Not even me!!!
Why are you broken?

steps.speaker: Military Doctor
steps.content: ...I don't need vindication, treatment, salvation, or anyone's forgiveness. There's only one thing I want to know...

steps.speaker: Military Doctor
steps.content: General, will you return to the battlefield? Are you still going to hunt those bastards down and make them pay?

steps.speaker: Military Doctor
steps.content: I will follow you with my Rancor to the ends of the earth, and we will slaughter every last one of them.
Why can't I die?

steps.speaker: Lieutenant
steps.content: ...Why do you still try to save me? What's left to salvage in a demon?

steps.speaker: Lieutenant
steps.content: Death would be a mercy. Just let me bear my punishment! I carry hell with me wherever I go anyway!
Why can't you just come back...?

steps.speaker: Iron Mask
steps.content: The Marshal said that if he fell, I was to follow you. That you would seize victory for him.

steps.speaker: Iron Mask
steps.content: ...I know you will. He had waited long enough. Bring him the true victory he was owed.
Victory? What kind of victory?
She had been awakened merely to officiate a funeral, one that felt far too long, arriving after her thirty-year absence.
A funeral for the very ones she had once believed were unbreakable.
[Grave]

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: We said when I woke up, I'd either help him fight his wars or give him a proper send-off.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: ...Never pegged the old grouch for the sentimental type.

steps.speaker: Commander-in-Chief
steps.content: The Eclipse Operation did cripple the Underground, but the Mania spread is irreversible. Paradeisos has ordered me to take command of the FAC. But one man is not an army.

steps.speaker: Commander-in-Chief
steps.content: Will you stay? The Commander's title is yours if that's what it takes.

steps.speaker: Commander-in-Chief
steps.content: After all, countless good soldiers have died to protect this city-state. Brock was one. Dravyn was another.
City-state... Before her slumber, this word could stir the blood of countless people. Now, it failed to cause even the slightest ripple in her heart.
Augustus lowered her head, her gaze falling upon the name etched into the tombstone.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Old man... you served him longer than I did. You knew the man he was...

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Tell me... what changed him into this?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Was it Mania? That same crystal flower that took Martin, Tom, Joe, Vennon, and his entire squad... Did it finally claim him, too?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Or was it that Undergrounder, "Parma"? Did he put a curse on him?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Tell me... where should I point my blade? Who is my enemy?

steps.speaker: Commander-in-Chief
steps.content: Dravyn was not a man to be broken by Mania. No matter what changes, every choice he ever made, in his eyes, served a single purpose. And he never regretted it.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Heh, you're right... The man was as stubborn as rust. All he cared about was protecting DisCity.
She tilted her head back without a word, her gaze fixed on the sky—or perhaps on the colossal form looming beneath it—for a long, silent moment...

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: ...So in the end, he was defeated by this... great city-state?
Adrian jolted alert, his hand flying to his gun.

steps.speaker: Commander-in-Chief
steps.content: ...When I accepted this rank, I accepted the duty that comes with it.

steps.speaker: Commander-in-Chief
steps.content: Do not force my hand, Augustus. Do not make me your enemy.
Those words drew the first hearty laugh from Augustus since her awakening.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Hahahaha... Relax, old man! What's a general without her blade? I can't even make sense of the last thirty years. Now's not the time!

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Those soldiers shipped off to the farlands for "resource acquisition," the people fed lies about justice and honor... and the units deliberately transferred to weaken the DisCorps...

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: After DisCorps fell, they were abandoned too, weren't they? How many units? Where are they? How many still draw breath? I'm going to find them back.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: My precious Reapers... shattered, rusted, and scattered to forgotten corners of the world. I won't let them wait in vain... I will find every last one, and bring them home.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: And then...
The razor-sharp edge returned to her eyes.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: I'm not you, Adrian. This isn't my city-state. I don't pledge to flags or thrones. My loyalty is only to the blade in my hand.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: When I return, this city-state had better give me a reason to stand down. If it doesn't... you'll need every gun you have to stop my blade from claiming what it owes.

<size=40>In late N.F. 103, Catherine Augustus Andohar—General of the Eighth DisCorps Division and the Independence Army's most elite soldier—abandoned DisCity. Her forces were a shadow of their former selves, their supplies nearly exhausted.

<size=40>The fracturing of DisCorps awakened old ambitions in the farlands. Enemies who had long coveted the city-state began to stir once again, and three years later, they succeeded in detonating a catastrophe at the world's very heart. The war that followed was brief, ending in a year, but it left in its wake the enduring blight of the Black Rings and catastrophes that scarred the globe.

With the end of the Marshal's iron rule, history's shame and glory were buried together. Grand ideals were dismantled, replaced by the seductive rallying cries of those now in power. Society found its solace in pleasurable apathy and decadent revelry. Under the glow of the Black Rings, madness marched steadily toward death.
<size=40>But Augustus no longer cared.

<size=40>She had forsaken the city-state. For over a decade since, she and her loyal subordinates have walked only the brutal, bloody path of warfare—far from prosperity and light, on a perpetual expedition toward hell.

steps.speaker: Rancor
steps.content: ...Are you going to stop us or judge us? Haha... Salvation? Where can we return to? A soldier's lover is their enemy!

steps.speaker: Rancor
steps.content: Bloodlust is glory, violence is justice, ignorance makes us unyielding, and hatred... hatred is the finest quality of all! It ignites our blood, circulating endlessly... endlessly! It is my eternal life! Brat, do you dare defy me?!

steps.speaker: Rancor
steps.content: Then strike me down, crush me, defeat me, destroy me, kill me countless times! Let the slaughter forge you countless times until you wield our remains to slay your enemies! Your strength is what we seek. Come!
[Slashing Effect]

This was the fate of the mightiest soldiers. For their convictions, they wielded the Rancors to kill. And when those beliefs were shattered, they were devoured by the very blades they carried, becoming mere instruments of war. Augustus conquered them. She tamed them. But more often than not, when she could not save them, she broke them all and laid them to rest.
They were beyond salvation. So many were beyond salvation. And this cursed funeral was nowhere near its end.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: They don't understand... You don't either... not yet... but...

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: When you truly hold power, when you reach the summit... on that day, you'll be no different...

steps.speaker: Rancor
steps.content: If you come for me, if you wish to save me, then bring us redemption through war! Comfort us with the blood of the enemy! Fight for vengeance, fight for DisCity! Or...

steps.speaker: Rancor
steps.content: Tell us who your enemies are, and we shall fight for you!!

steps.speaker: Rancor
steps.content: Take us with you, General. The Rancors desire you. Take us to hell back to the battlefield!!

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: ...Do not come back...

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: Catherine... never... come back...
[Empty scene for 1 second, fade to black, then sudden screen flash]

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: ...That's only you! Pathetic losers!

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: I swear, no matter what enemy I face, once I step onto the battlefield, I will not retreat. I will not falter. I will not surrender. I will rise every time I fall—until victory is won, or I meet a glorious death!

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: I. Will. Never. Become. You!!!

She charged headlong into the abyss, her mortal legs wading through swamps of flesh and blood. Let the shadows of war envelop her. Let the frenzied souls of the dead tear at her flesh. This was what she had been born for!
Lost time could not be reclaimed, so she pursued death itself to recover the fallen. She had awakened now, and this time, she chose her own battlefield.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Soldiers of DisCorps who were abandoned and have lost your way... let your Rancors shut up and listen to me.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: From this moment, I am your only commander. You will follow my orders, and mine alone. You will fight only on the battlefields I choose.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: And in return... I will bear the weight of your sins. I will chart your path forward. I will restore your glory.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: You will not be asked to compromise your duty. You will not be ordered to make pointless sacrifices. You will have your justice, your honor, and your win. All of it. Every battle you fight under my command will be honorable, with not a single blemish on your victory!

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: ...My exploited, broken, abandoned soldiers... Your hell ends now. Come with me. It is time to return to the world of the living.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: My blades—in victory or defeat, in life or in death—will always be human.
<color=#7683a2><size=40>The general plunged into hell, while history marched on regardless.

<color=#7683a2><size=40>Perhaps her blade would carve a path to power's pinnacle, reclaiming glory through violence.
Then, like all who came before, she would have that very strength corrupted, her iron will hollowed out, swinging her blade against the chaos until she finally fell from her throne.

<color=#7683a2><size=40>Perhaps her conquest would cower the dead and smother the embers of past wars.
But for the hatreds sown too deep to root out, she could only conquer on. Every land she crossed would be stained by her influence, as she herself became stained with blood.

<color=#7683a2><size=40>Or perhaps...
The general would fall in battle, lost on the road home, meeting the same meaningless end as the countless souls she had once reaped.

Born for war, to die in battle would be the most fitting and natural conclusion—before her strength could carve a path into even greater torrents.

<color=#7683a2><size=40>Or maybe...

Perhaps someday, in a distant future, by the slimmest chance imaginable...
<color=#3877E0><size=40>Even one who had lived an entire life by the blade would meet a truly unremarkable end.
[Cemetery] (Return to present day)

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Heh, I came back after all, you old bastards. Angry enough to climb out of your graves?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Now that everyone's here, I can show you something good.
For years, the names of the two previous commanders have rested in silence upon their tombstones. As she looks up, a faint gray silhouette emerges from the short distance, moving toward her.

options: I came to see the blade that returned.

choices.text: I came to see the blade that returned.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I heard that an exceptional weapon is priceless. It only stays sharp because it's cared for.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Still not broken yet? Need any tending?

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Don't worry. Everything's fine.

steps.speaker: Augustus
steps.content: Now the blade can finally return to its scabbard.
